name: unIIcode
description: Inventing new characters to fill the gaps in Unicode. Exhibited at PROMPT: Design × AI, Shenzhen (2026).

text: The [unicode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicode) is a text encoding standard used by most modern computers to support 161 scripts used by the world's major writing systems.

Unicode encoding contains gaps between scripts and ensures that a new script starts from a '00'. This allows for new characters to be added to existing scripts without having to disrupt other scripts.
Since 2021, I have been training machine learning models to invent characters for these gaps: glyphs that belong to a script, but that no one has ever written.

The latest iteration learns from every assigned glyph in Unicode, over 100,000 characters drawn as 128×128 images. A script-conditioned diffusion model learns what each script looks like, then invents a glyph for each empty code point in the style of its neighbours.
Printed in full, it becomes an alphabet of the gaps: about 120 pages, with the real characters in grey and the invented ones in red.

text: A second model, a conditional variational autoencoder, maps every glyph into one shared shape space. Moving through it morphs one script into another: the same letter, written as if it were Greek, Devanagari, Tamil or Thai.

sections.alt: A tour of the shape space, one Unicode block at a time, each block's characters joined by a red line

text: A tour through that shape space, one Unicode block at a time. The red line joins the block's characters in code-point order, tracing how one script's letters spread out among every other script's.

unIIcode was invited by the Shenzhen Graphic Design Association to its international exhibition [PROMPT: Design × AI](https://www.sgda.cc/news-event/news/news/94.html), in the "AI for Design" section. K11 HACC, Shenzhen, July 25 – October 25, 2026.
It is shown as four large-format scroll prints, each 594 × 1782 mm, on Decor Etching 170 gsm paper mounted on aluminum panels.

This character does not exist in any language. It was created by the ML model.
To train the model, I created 128*128 pixel PNGs of all the characters.
The Tamil script was used to generate more Tamil characters.
These were then 3D modeled and printed to create physical characters.
